topic: Can we stop global climate change?

primary_direction.name: CO-FET
primary_direction.expanded_name: Climate Observing and Flexible Energy Transition
primary_direction.claim: A coordinated data-to-decision policy can reduce worst-case regret and residual climate risk while preserving reliability, affordability, and equity better than single-objective alternatives across plausible futures.
primary_direction.research_object: Policy portfolio evaluated in a scenario ensemble, not a single climate forecast.
primary_direction.falsification: Reject the direction if it fails to outperform carbon-only or technology-only policies on held-out worst-case regret under equal physical constraints, or if its advantage depends on perfect observations or hidden exclusions.

candidate_routes.name: observation-first
candidate_routes.weakness: Does not specify near-term mitigation and flexibility decisions

candidate_routes.name: technology-only
candidate_routes.weakness: Can ignore uncertainty, distributional burden, and grid bottlenecks

candidate_routes.name: carbon-removal-first
candidate_routes.weakness: Depends on uncertain permanence, land, water, monitoring, and future scale

candidate_routes.name: CO-FET
candidate_routes.strength: Couples observation, risk, flexibility, equity, and adaptive decisions
candidate_routes.weakness: More data, governance, and computational coordination are required

predictions: Robust portfolios diversify generation and flexibility resources.
Decision-linked observation upgrades reduce regret when they alter actions.
Mean-emissions optimization can fail reliability or distributional tests.
Pre-declared staged triggers improve adaptation to scenario uncertainty.
